title: Auth API Contracts
note: All request bodies and response shapes are validated at runtime via Fastify Ajv (Constitution Principle VII). Shared type definitions live in packages/core/src/types/auth.ts.

endpoints.summary: Exchange a Google ID token for a server-issued session JWT
endpoints.serverValidation: Signature, expiry, audience (all values in GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS), and email_verified: true. Tokens failing any check → 401 INVALID_GOOGLE_TOKEN.

idToken.description: Google ID token obtained from the native Google Sign-In SDK on mobile

200.description: Sign-in successful. Returns the session JWT and basic user info.

token.description: Server-issued session JWT. Store in platform secure storage. Send as Authorization: Bearer <token> on subsequent requests.

400.description: Validation error — request body is malformed or idToken is missing.

401.description: The Google ID token is invalid, expired, does not match the expected audience, or email_verified is false.

endpoints.summary: Acknowledge sign-out (server-side no-op; client deletes stored token)
endpoints.authentication: Bearer session JWT (optional — succeeds even if no token present)
endpoints.note: Session JWTs are stateless; sign-out is implemented by the mobile deleting the stored token. This endpoint exists to provide a clean API boundary and a hook for future server-side revocation if needed. There is currently no server-side revocation mechanism — the 7-day TTL is the only safeguard against a stolen token. Acceptable for personal use; revisit if scope grows.
endpoints.pluginBehavior: The auth plugin must not throw on an absent or malformed Authorization header. Route handlers receive a guest identity and decide whether to return 401.

endpoints.summary: Return the current user's profile, or guest identity if unauthenticated
endpoints.pluginBehavior: The auth plugin must not throw on an absent or malformed Authorization header. Returns guest identity when no valid token is present.

200.description: Current identity — either authenticated user or guest.

errorCodes.INVALID_GOOGLE_TOKEN: Google ID token is invalid, expired, or wrong audience
errorCodes.UNAUTHORIZED: Request requires authentication but no valid token was supplied

authScheme.secretSource: SESSION_JWT_SECRET environment variable (never baked into container image)
authScheme.revocation: None — JWTs are stateless. A compromised token remains valid until expiry (up to 7 days). Acceptable for personal use. If revocation is ever needed, introduce a server-side allowlist/denylist keyed on the token's jti claim.
authScheme.audienceValidation: The full GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS list (comma-separated env var) must be passed as the audience parameter to OAuth2Client.verifyIdToken(). This is the primary defence against token substitution attacks.
